source.title: Cordia subcordata (Boraginaceae), a distylous species on oceanic coral islands, is self-compatible and pollinated by a passerine bird

source_routes.publisher_article: Plant Ecology and Evolution / Pensoft article 24681
source_routes.open_pdf_mirror: Semantic Scholar open PDF matching the article DOI/title
source_routes.checksum_boundary: Public exact article bytes are identifiable and readable, but no repository checksum is recorded yet; do not mark byte-level provenance complete.

response_channel.interpretation_boundary: The between-island floral response is loss/extreme skew of a floral morph state, not a flower-size compression estimate. The paper does not identify the cause of the morph-ratio difference.

reproductive_outcome_channel.interpretation_boundary: The natural fruit-set contrast is an outcome difference. It does not by itself identify pollinator causation because the two islands differ in other ecological and demographic attributes.

pollination_treatments.hand_inter_morph: performed; seed set comparable to other hand treatments

dependency_channel.source_native_reading: The species is self-compatible under hand self-pollination but does not autonomously set fruit/seed when bagged without pollen transfer, indicating strong dependence on a pollen vector under the tested Yongxing conditions.
dependency_channel.critical_missing_link: Equivalent controlled dependency treatments were not reported for Dong Island, where morph loss, low visitation and low natural fruit set were observed.

pollinator_environment_channel.boundary: The island difference in visitation is descriptive and not a randomized exposure.

effective_service_channel.design: Virgin inflorescences were bagged, uncovered for exactly one visit, then stigmas were collected and pollen grains counted.
effective_service_channel.critical_missing_link: Single-visit pollen deposition was measured at Yongxing, not Dong. Dong therefore lacks the matched per-visit effectiveness measurement needed to identify whether its lower natural fruit set is caused by lower effective service.

bridge_assessment.why_near_complete_not_complete: The paper contains all required channel types, but the strongest mechanistic measurements are asymmetric: controlled breeding and single-visit pollen deposition are from Yongxing, whereas Dong supplies the extreme morph-ratio state, low visitation and low natural fruit set. Without Dong single-visit effectiveness and controlled dependency treatments, the response transition cannot be linked end-to-end at matched population level.
bridge_assessment.allowed_claim: Cordia subcordata is the strongest external near-complete mechanism bridge currently identified: within one source-defined two-island system, floral morph-state divergence, pollinator-environment differences, direct single-visit pollen function and controlled reproductive dependence are all observed. The system supports the plausibility of the proposed mechanism architecture but does not identify the causal chain across the Yongxing-Dong contrast.
blocked_claims: do not call the Dong morph loss a pollinator-caused evolutionary response
do not transport Yongxing single-visit effectiveness numerically to Dong
do not transport Yongxing bagging/self-pollination dependency numerically to Dong
do not equate self-compatibility with autonomous reproductive assurance
do not treat natural fruit-set differences as an effective-service effect
do not call this bridge_system_complete until both sides of the response contrast have matched effectiveness and dependency evidence
do not open formal cross-system mechanism fitting from this system alone

next_actions: Checksum-lock the exact CC-BY article bytes in the source registry.
Search for Dong Island controlled bagging/hand-pollination data or later follow-up experiments using the same population.
Search for Dong Island single-visit pollen deposition or another direct visitor-effectiveness measure.
If both missing Dong channels remain unavailable, preserve Cordia as near-complete partial evidence rather than weakening the matched-population rule.
Only after matched two-sided effectiveness and dependency data exist should a causal Yongxing-Dong mechanism contrast be considered.
